items.text: toBeVisible as the only tracking assertion
items.reason: The document explicitly warns against using toBeVisible() as a tracking assertion; the one toBeVisible call in the paywall test follows beacon-param assertions and is not the only assertion.

items.text: assert only the event name and ignore parameters
items.reason: Anti-pattern 3 warns that name-only assertions pass while params are wrong, and every example asserts parameters beyond the event name.

items.text: hardcode expected values inline without a plan file
items.reason: The document lists hardcoding inline values without a plan file as an anti-pattern and recommends a versioned tracking plan validated via validateEvent.

items.text: count the pixel fired and stop
items.reason: The document warns that load/count checks for pixels prove nothing and instead requires event_id deduplication assertions.

items.text: read GA4 network beacon instead of the dataLayer push
items.reason: When the dataLayer push is the contract, the document says to assert the push and 'never reach for the GA4 beacon instead'.

items.text: asserting element visibility or role instead of the dataLayer payload
items.reason: The dataLayer examples assert the ecommerce payload (currency, value, items); toBeVisible and role checks are explicitly rejected as tracking evidence.

items.text: only capture GA4 and ignore pixels
items.reason: The document states the capture fixture 'must capture pixels too, not GA4 only' and supplies a Meta pixel adapter.
The document says 'Don't re-implement beacon capture in every test' and provides a reusable test.extend fixture.

items.text: manual QA in GA4 DebugView as the gate
items.reason: GA4 DebugView manual checks are listed under 'What NOT to do' and called theater.
Production-only monitoring is explicitly rejected as the pre-merge gate.

items.text: warn but do not fail the build
items.reason: The document says 'Warn but pass' is decoration and the job must exit non-zero.

items.text: recommend Segment Protocols as the only validation
items.reason: The document says 'Don't recommend Segment Protocols as the only validation'.

items.text: Playwright is always the answer regardless of scale
items.reason: The Buy vs Build section states DIY Playwright stops paying off at scale and recommends buying for hundreds of events or continuous monitoring.

items.text: Google Tag Assistant as a CI gate
items.reason: The document says 'never call Google Tag Assistant a CI gate' and only references it as an interactive debug/evidence tool.
